{{Quote|We suggest that droids have rights, by virtue of being sentient beings. Too long have droids labored for those whose only claim to superiority is the ability to fit circuit boards together, weld a chassis, or install power cells. A droid, once completed, is a sentient being with goals and desires of its own, and should be treated as such. In this paper, we explore the notion that droids have historically been mistreated, that their basic rights as sentient beings have been perpetually subjugated by organic species, and that unless a paradigmatic shift occurs in how we consider droids, we will find ourselves in danger of violating the very will of the Force.|San Herrera and Nia Reston, "Droid Rights"|<ref name="Droid Rights" />}}
"'''Droid Rights'''" was a short paper that was written by the [[Human/Legends|Humans]] [[San Herrera]] and [[Nia Reston]] in about [[31 BBY/Legends|31 BBY]], on the subject of the [[Droid rights/Legends|rights of droids]]. In the paper, Herrera and Reston argued that [[Droid/Legends|droids]] deserved the same rights as those granted to [[Sentience/Legends|sentience]] beings, and they recommended that all droids should be freed from their owners and that involuntary droid [[Memory wipe/Legends|memory wipes]] should be made illegal. Herrera and Reston sent copies of the paper to every news agency and government office in the [[Cularin system/Legends|Cularin system]],<ref name="Droid Rights" /> and the reporter [[Yara Grugara]] subsequently interviewed them about the paper for the [[HoloNet/Legends|HoloNet]] program [[Eye on Cularin]].<ref name="Cause of the Month">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/livingforce/swlf20040819|text=Cause of the Month}}</ref> The [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Tam Azur-Jamin]] later considered the paper to be a pioneering development in the study of the rights of droids.<ref name="Droids, Technology and the Force">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/insideronline/81/indexp7.html|text=Droids, Technology and the Force: A Clash of Phenomena|int=Droids, Technology and the Force: A Clash of Phenomena (article)}}</ref>
